utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone in and around this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, everyone. This is case IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Before we hear the testimony of the next witness, I have a few procedural matters which I would like to deal with. The first is about the urgent Stanisic motion for equality of arms and immediate suspension of the trial, with the annexes attached to it. The motion was filed on the 1st of February, 2011. In relation to the Stanisic Defence's request for the Chamber to quash the Registry's finding -- funding decisions in this case and to compel the Registry to provide adequate resources to facilitate a fair trial pursuant to Article 20 and 21 of this Statute, the Chamber hereby invites the -- invites OLAD to make any submissions on this issue by close of business on Tuesday, the 8th of February, 2011. In relation to Stanisic Defence request for suspension of all aspects of the trial process, other than the examination of the remaining Prosecution witnesses, the Chamber hereby invites the Prosecution to indicate today in court whether it seeks to respond to specifically this part of the motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The Prosecution does, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When do you think that you would be able to file your response?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Before the end of this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before the end of this week. Then I move to the next item. I take it, Mr. Registrar, that OLAD will be informed about the invitation and about the dead-line. We then move on to Witness JF-030. The Chamber would like to receive written submissions from the parties on the possibilities the Chamber may have to rely on non-attested parts of the statement of Witness JF-030. Any indication as to when you could make such submissions? It's not the most urgent matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would say one week from today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if acceptable to you, we seek ten days, which means until the end of next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ten days is granted. Mr. Jordash?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The same, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ten days is granted to the Stanisic Defence as well. Then I finally would deal with some issues relating to the documents which were marked for identification and which were presented in relation to the report of the Expert Theunens, and especially those tendered by the Simatovic Defence, documents which are listed in a table annexed to the filing of the 24th of November of 2010. There is -- among these documents, there is a series which, to say it short, are documents collected by the Defence investigator from a potential Defence witness. I list them briefly. That is D167, D174, D182, D185 through D193, and D195. I did not mention D146, which would fall into this category. But you find D146, although with the same problem, already on the list of questions that was submitted to the parties by the Chamber for the next housekeeping session, and you find it listed under number 16. These documents I just mentioned are objected by the Prosecution because they have not received further information on the source, although for some of them there are other reasons of objection as well, but I focus at this moment on this reason. The issue of the lack of information on the source was addressed on the 27th of January in relation to D190 MFI after the Simatovic Defence used D190 MFI with a witness, transcript pages 10785 up to and including -789. And on this occasion, the Prosecution indicated that it was willing to withdraw its objections if information on the source could be provided, even off the record, at least that it would consider to then withdraw its objections, of course always depending on the content of the information. The Chamber would like to know whether the Simatovic Defence has the requested -- have provided the information on the source requested by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, pursuant to our instructions, I contacted Mr. Groome on the break and gave him information from whom we got that, and Mr. Groome said he would check or, rather, compare the signature on that document to other signatures by Mr. Karadzic and then that he would make public his position, but we haven't had feedback since.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I haven't had an opportunity to compare the signature of D190 yet with other known signatures of Dr. Karadzic, but that is something I could do relatively quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When could we hear from you?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Tomorrow, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Tomorrow. Then, the next category was the documents which were received pursuant to the Defence request for assistance dated the 10th of March, 2008. I list them: It's D183 and D195. And the Prosecution has objected to admission of these documents until it has received from the Simatovic Defence a copy of the 10th of March, 2008, RFA response. Has the Simatovic Defence provided a copy of the RFA response to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will check during the break with my Case Manager. We asked them a couple of days ago to compile all the RAFs [as interpreted], and then I will give you information whether these sets are complete and ready. But we have certainly done everything to collect all the RAFs to be able to submit them as required.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I don't know whether you asked for all of them but at least for the RFAs in relation to D183 and D195. When do you think you could provide that information finally? I mean, that you are preparing it, this is highly appreciated but does not enable Mr. Groome yet to give us his opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I know. I received a communication, written communication, from Mr. Groome. It's a list of about 20 documents, I believe, in which -- with regard to which they request assistance from us. But I believe that we have given everything, not only D183 and D195, but everything they requested. But during the break I will contact our Case Manager to see what exactly the state of affairs is. And if anything has not been sent to Mr. Groome yet, I'll make sure it is sent soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, could you make the same effort to analyse what you've received and perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, we've been trying to take a close look at this, this material, towards the end of our case and Ms. Marcus has been doing this and she believes we have not received this material yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Could we then -- if you would please verify together during the break what's missing, and then we'll hear from you when you'll be able to give the Chamber your final position in relation to D185 and D195. I have no further procedural matters on my list. Is there any other matter? Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's concerning our application to suspend. It's really this: That there are two dead-lines this week. One is to get back to the Trial Chamber concerning the subpoena issue in relation to JF-051, and the other is a dead-line for this Friday, 4th of February, which is in response to the Prosecution's 20th application to add to the 65 ter exhibit list. Would it be acceptable to the Chamber to adjourn those dates until, say, next week when Your Honours have received the response or the views from the Prosecution? At the very least, a delay would be extremely helpful to us. And if Your Honours are eventually with us in terms of suspension, then our application will have -- well, it will not thwart the purpose of our application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, just as a practical matter, this I'll put in my submission, but it occurred to me last night, and I've only been able to give Mr. Jordash's lengthy submission a cursory view because of other obligations, but it seems to me that Mr. Knoops is still a co-counsel on the case and it seems like these types of written applications are -- is he not in a position to assist Mr. Jordash? I have no qualms with the pressure that Mr. Jordash is under, but it seems that there is a co-counsel in the case and can he not be of service until he is finally discharged, if he is discharged, from the case?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, I know that an explanation for the discontinuation of his then-position as lead counsel is one of the attachments to your submission, but could you please briefly respond to Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: In this way, I'll respond, Your Honours: Firstly, Mr. Knoops stopped working at the time we took on our consultant who is proposed to be a co-counsel. It was explained to OLAD at the time that as a consequence of the funding it simply wasn't possible for Mr. Knoops to continue. And he had other commitments which would pay him a reasonable living income. And so the position we're in now is that he, Mr. Knoops, isn't engaged in the case and I don't know what his working schedule is at the moment. But I know that his position, which I accept is reasonable, is that he needs to earn a living, and working on this case doesn't do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's not at length discuss what that means, but the Chamber was informed that you would be lead counsel, Mr. Knoops would be co-counsel. The Chamber at that time was not informed, at least not by you, if I understand you well, that Mr. Knoops would not take any further activity in the case. Which, of course, comes a bit as a surprise if someone is still at the -- still in the team mentioned as being co-counsel. I mean, that whatever internal matters may have caused this is another issue, but if I also understood the situation well, that one of the reasons why Mr. Knoops would remain co-counsel was that there was a fear that there was a risk of discontinuity in the dealing with the case. Now if you tell me that Mr. Knoops didn't work on the case anymore but he was left on the list as co-counsel, which gives the impression that he is involved in the case, and then without any further explanation we hear a couple of months later that he is not on the case anymore, let me say the least that this is surprising information under the present circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, if I can explain that a little further. I probably overstated the case in one sense. Mr. Knoops has a very discrete job which he is working n and he does that on a pro-bono basis; it's not directly concerning the substance of the case, nor is it concerning procedural issues such as motions. It's something to do with the investigation. But the situations arose because when we went to OLAD and explained the situation, and I and Mr. Knoops requested that Mr. Gosnell be made co-counsel and confirmed he was ready, OLAD refused that application and said, Well, despite that, we want Mr. Knoops to remain as co-counsel, despite the fact that you've told us that his role is now going to be that of a consultant; and we told OLAD precisely what that discrete role was going to be. Despite that, they refused to allow him to be re-assigned as a consultant and refused to allow Mr. Gosnell to be co-counsel and set a time-period, initially three to four months, before Mr. Gosnell could be a co-counsel and then, I think, eventually settled on three months. That time-period, I don't know why that time-period was chosen but it was against what both Mr. Knoops and I were saying is knowledge -- consistent with his knowledge of the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The matter may need further attention. Let's focus at this moment on what you asked, that is, to -- for two dead-lines. The first one, subpoena issue in relation to Witness JF-051, and the second one --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- is the Friday the 4th of February dead-line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The 20th application - I'm a bad bookkeeper - is about --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- admission of -- I think it's either addition to the 65 ter list or admission of the evidence as exhibits. I forget which one. But it's one of those, relating to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, could you help us out? I could check that and find it on my computer if need be, but if you could tell me, then ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe it's the additional excerpts from the notebooks. I have someone checking it now. If I'm wrong, I'll stand up again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's the 47 pages from where you gave notice that you wanted to use them and you wanted to ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or is that -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It's not the Mladic notebooks. It's the Pecanac and Banja Luka evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Oh. Then I am familiar with this. It's, again, a relatively small collection. One of them we're not asking for anything other than to have them MFI'd; and the other, I forget the exact number of pages but I think it's somewhere in the order of 30 pages. But I can get precise information in a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, the dead-lines for this week are moved forward to Monday noon next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not that the Chamber doesn't understand there's a lot of work to be done. That's -- don't understand this wrongly. But that is our decision. And for the -- if I could say the great suspension, the Chamber will pay very specific and thorough attention to that. These are not matters which you can decide in five or seven minutes. One of the complications perhaps also being that of course today the president has delivered a decision on -- at least I've seen a decision on the -- on the matter also related to funding. So therefore we'd like to look at that and we'd like to look at all the annexes, we want to hear OLAD. Meanwhile, we accommodate you perhaps not very much but at least give you a time until after the weekend. Any other matter? If not, then for the next witness we move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I may take it that we might have to go into private session soon, Mr. Groome, but I wanted to clearly make -- I wanted to make it clear that we have now finished with the closed session testimony of the witness. I was informed that -- the Chamber was informed that you wanted to make submissions but on a matter which makes it likely that you would like to do it in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are now in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. For one moment, Mr. Petrovic, I thought you would offer your apologies to the interpreters for not having waited until tomorrow in giving your apologies to me and to the Chamber and to all the others. We adjourn until tomorrow, Thursday, the 3rd of February, quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon, this same Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 3rd day of February, 2011, at 2.15 p.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.06 p.m.,
